title: Planning a Class Debate
text:
A debate outline helps speakers organise their ideas before the event. It usually begins with a clear statement of the topic. Each speaker then lists the main arguments and the evidence that supports them. Good outlines also include possible questions from the other side.

For example, a team arguing that schools should start later might list sleep research as evidence. They could prepare a short answer to the claim that students would finish school later. Teachers often ask students to write the outline before they practise. This makes the final debate more organised and easier to follow.

questions.text: What does a debate outline usually begin with?
options: A clear statement of the topic
A short summary of the winner
A set of questions for the judge

questions.text: What kind of evidence might a team arguing for a later school start use?
Why do teachers ask students to write the outline before they practise?
options: To make the debate more organised
To choose the winner in advance

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain how to prepare a debate outline

vocabulary.definition: a short plan or summary of the main points
facts or information that show something is true
reasons given to support or oppose an idea
arranged in a clear and logical way

paragraph_translations: Um esboço de debate ajuda os oradores a organizar suas ideias antes do evento. Ele geralmente começa com uma declaração clara do tema. Em seguida, cada orador lista os principais argumentos e as evidências que os apoiam. Bons esboços também incluem possíveis perguntas do outro lado.

Por exemplo, uma equipe que defende que as escolas devem começar mais tarde pode usar pesquisas sobre sono como evidência. Ela poderia preparar uma resposta curta para a afirmação de que os alunos terminariam a escola mais tarde. Os professores costumam pedir aos alunos que escrevam o esboço antes de praticar. Isso torna o debate final mais organizado e fácil de acompanhar.
